intro.lead: Muster is a local-first coordination client built on Logos. A group opens a room, agrees what to do, and does it, with privacy proven at every step.
body: It runs inside Logos Basecamp, and keeps a transparent record of exposure at every step.
Muster uses Basecamp to plug into other modules built on Logos, including Delivery, the Logos Execution Zone, Logos Storage, and RLN.

Logos modules behind every room, loaded on demand by Basecamp.
Stages of a transaction, each one shown as it happens.

room.title: What is Muster?
body: Muster is a local-first client for coordinating actions between several people inside a conversation. A group splits a bill, runs a shared wallet or shares files, and every proposal, approval and payment is agreed in the room.
The room is peer-to-peer, with no clouds or accounts required. Members propose actions as cards, check exactly what they would be signing, and approve with their own keys.
It is an educational tool under ongoing development. Walk through the whole lifecycle of a multi-party transaction and learn, at each step, what stays private and where data leaks.

basecamp.title: Built on Basecamp
body: Muster runs on Basecamp, a local-first launcher for peer-to-peer apps built on Logos.
Basecamp loads modules for Muster, installing apps and the functions they need through its package manager. There is no hosted frontend and no signup. Everything lives on your device.

architecture.title: Built on Basecamp
body: Muster is two Basecamp modules: a core and an interface. The interface provides a self-hosted frontend for the application, while the core connects to other modules and uses Basecamp to load them in where needed.

modules.title: Powered by Logos
body: Every Muster room's communication is encrypted and served over Logos Delivery to its members. Keys rotate whenever someone joins or leaves, securing old data against new arrivals.

Everything the room does is written to a signed, hash-linked log that only members can read. Proposals, approvals, and payment reports are each an entry signed by their author. Every member's client rebuilds the room's state from that log, no servers required.
Payments settle on whichever chain the group chooses. On the Logos Execution Zone, a payment can be made private, where the chain records no payer, payee, or amount.

rooms.title: What you can do on Muster
body: Each Muster room is set up for what its members plan to do.
The tool is under active development, and it can already be used for a number of activities that need secure peer-to-peer coordination.

entries.title: Monero multisig wallet
body: Set up a 2-of-3 Monero multisig wallet from a Muster room, fund it, and coordinate the signing of transactions without an intermediary.
Each member's key stays in their own Monero wallet. Muster only facilitates the signing.

video.alt: Monero multisig demo showing a 2-of-3 wallet and a jointly approved payment in Muster

entries.title: Split the bill
body: Split a bill without routing your spending data through someone else's server. Members choose to split publicly or privately, on whatever chain they like, and settle in any combination of supported tokens.

video.alt: Split the bill demo showing a proposal, payment approval and settlement in Muster

entries.title: FileShare
body: Share files without storing them on a central server. A file is encrypted before it is stored, and only its content identifier is shared in the room.
Members retrieve it through Logos Storage, so files move privately without handing control to a server.

video.alt: FileShare demo showing a file sent and received in a Muster room

prifi.title: Muster makes PriFi visible.
body: To enable Private Finance (PriFi), primitives must be deployed on privacy‑preserving, peer‑to‑peer infrastructure, on hardware you control.
Every transaction has seven stages, from finding a counterparty to enforcing the deal, and it is only as strong as its weakest link. Secure settlement alone is not enough to ensure privacy.
Muster walks a group through those stages as they happen. It shows what stays inside the room at each step, what reaches a chain or a store node, and how a conventional stack handles the same step.

title: Basecamp is open
to all builders
body: Muster needed a modular framework for building privacy-preserving apps. Basecamp gives it the ability to easily deliver encrypted rooms, private settlement, and file-sharing in one app, running on each member's own machine.
